data.cultural_impact: The name Crispian holds a significant cultural impact by reminding us of the bravery and resilience of early Christian martyrs during the Roman Empire. Saint Crispin, born during the late 2nd or early 3rd century, lived and died for his faith. His story echoes the struggles and sacrifices made by many early Christians in the face of persecution.
data.spiritual_significance: Historically, the name Crispian has a powerful spiritual significance as it represents a deep commitment to faith, even when faced with opposition and persecution. It is a reminder of the steadfastness and unwavering belief in God, even during the most challenging times. It serves as an inspiration for all to remain steadfast in their faith and to follow the example set by the early Christian martyrs.

historical_references.reference: According to legend, Crispian was a martyr in the 3rd century who was converted to Christianity by Saint Alphege. He was a pagan nobleman who was won over by Alphege's teachings and was eventually put to death for his new faith. This event is commemorated on October 25 in the Roman Martyrology.
historical_references.context: Legendary martyr who converted to Christianity under the tutelage of Saint Alphege and was later put to death for his new faith.

historical_references.reference: In the Hagiography of St. Crispin and St. Crispian, written in the 12th century, the two saints Crispin and Crispian are described as brothers and shoemakers who, during the persecutions of Diocletian, were tortured and killed for refusing to abandon their faith. The two saints are considered the patron saints of shoemakers and horsemen.
historical_references.context: Legendary martyrs and shoemakers who were tortured and killed during the persecutions of Diocletian for refusing to abandon their Christian faith.
